faqs.q: Does the counter include spaces in the character count?
faqs.a: Both figures are shown. Characters with spaces counts every keystroke including spaces and line breaks; characters without spaces excludes whitespace. Forms usually specify which one they mean — if not, assume with spaces.

faqs.q: How is reading time calculated?
faqs.a: Words divided by 238 words per minute, the widely cited average silent reading speed for adults. Speaking time uses 130 words per minute. Both are rounded to the nearest sensible unit and are estimates, not promises.

faqs.q: How does my word processor get a different count?
faqs.a: Word processors disagree on hyphenated words, abbreviations, numbers, emoji and trailing punctuation. Microsoft Word counts a hyphenated compound as one word; some tools count it as two. If a limit is strict, check which convention the recipient uses.

faqs.q: What is Title Case?
faqs.a: Title case capitalises the first and last words and all major words, while leaving short articles, conjunctions and prepositions lowercase unless they come first. So: The Man Who Knew Too Much, not The Man who Knew too Much.

faqs.q: Which case should I use for URLs and file names?
faqs.a: kebab-case for URLs and CSS class names, because search engines treat hyphens as word separators. snake_case is conventional for database columns, JSON keys and Python variables. Avoid spaces in any of them.

faqs.q: What is Sentence case?
faqs.a: Sentence case capitalises only the first letter of each sentence and any proper nouns — the style used by most British newspapers and the GOV.UK design system. It is easier to read than title case for long headings.

faqs.q: Does converting case change the words?
faqs.a: No. Only letter case changes, except in camel, Pascal, snake, kebab and constant modes, which also replace spaces with formatting characters and remove punctuation as part of building a valid identifier.

disclaimer: Converted identifiers are not checked against reserved words in your programming language.
editorial_note: The developer cases are included because copy-pasting a headline into code and fixing it by hand is a common time sink.

faqs.q: How is daylight saving handled?
faqs.a: The browser's Intl API uses the IANA time zone database, so each city's offset is calculated for the specific date you choose, including transition dates. That is why the same pair of cities can be four hours apart in March and five hours apart in April.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a time zone and an offset?
faqs.a: A time zone is a region with a set of rules, such as Europe/London, which switches between GMT and BST. An offset is a fixed number such as UTC+1. Booking systems that ask for an offset instead of a zone are where recurring meetings usually break.

faqs.q: Why do some places not observe daylight saving?
faqs.a: Most of Asia, Africa and the tropics do not shift, because the daylight benefit is small near the equator. China uses a single zone across five geographic zones. Japan and India do not observe daylight saving.

faqs.q: How do I find a meeting time that works for everyone?
faqs.a: Start with the city that has the most constrained working hours, usually the furthest east or west, then slide the source time until that city is inside 09:00–17:00. If no overlap exists at all, an asynchronous update or a rotating meeting time is more respectful than a 23:00 call.

disclaimer: Time zone rules come from your browser's database and can change if a government alters its rules; keep your browser current.
editorial_note: We highlight working hours rather than just listing offsets, because the practical question is whether a slot is reasonable, not merely what the clock says.

This checker uses a longest-common-subsequence comparison — the same family of algorithm as git diff — to mark every added and removed line, count them, and score how similar the two texts are. faqs.q: How does the comparison algorithm work?

faqs.q: What does the similarity percentage mean?
faqs.a: The share of compared lines that are unchanged. A 33% score means roughly two thirds of the lines differ in some way. It is an indicator of scale, not a measure of importance — a single changed word in a one-line contract clause can matter more than 100 changed lines of formatting.

faqs.q: Does compressing an image reduce quality?
faqs.a: JPEG and WebP compression is lossy, so some data is discarded. At quality 0.8 and a sensible resolution the difference is usually invisible on screen; the damage becomes visible in fine detail, gradients and text at low quality settings. PNG remains lossless, so re-encoding a PNG as PNG mainly helps through downscaling.

faqs.q: What size should I compress to?
faqs.a: For a website hero image, 1600 pixels wide is plenty. For an inline article image, 1000 to 1200 pixels. For a form that demands under 100 KB, reduce width first and quality second. Print needs far more: 300 DPI at the physical size.

faqs.q: Does this remove EXIF metadata?
faqs.a: Re-encoding through a canvas drops most metadata, including GPS location. That is usually desirable for images posted publicly, but it also removes orientation data, so images taken in portrait on a phone should be checked after compression.

faqs.q: Can I compress HEIC photos from an iPhone?
faqs.a: Not directly in most browsers, because Safari and Chrome do not decode HEIC consistently. Export the photo as JPEG from your phone's share sheet first, then compress it here.

disclaimer: Compression is lossy for JPEG and WebP output; keep your originals.
editorial_note: The width control matters more than the quality slider for hitting hard file-size limits, so both are exposed.

intro: JPG and PNG solve different problems. JPEG is a compressed format tuned for photographs, with no transparency. PNG is lossless and supports an alpha channel, which is why design tools, presentations and upload forms sometimes insist on it.

Converting JPEG to PNG cannot recover detail the JPEG already discarded — that information is gone. What it does achieve is a lossless file you can edit and re-save repeatedly without further degradation, plus a canvas that supports transparency if you add it later. faqs.q: Why is the PNG file so much larger?
faqs.a: JPEG discards information the eye is unlikely to notice, especially in smooth areas. PNG preserves every pixel, so photographic images compress poorly. Text and screenshots, which have large areas of flat colour, convert much more efficiently.

intro: PDF is the format people ask for when they want a document to look the same everywhere, but Word files are what most of us actually write in. Converting normally means uploading your CV, contract or report to a third-party service.

This converter reads the DOCX file in your browser, extracts its text with paragraph structure, and lays it out as a paginated PDF. It is honest about its limits: complex layout, images, tables, headers and custom fonts are not reproduced. For a straightforward text document it produces a clean, readable PDF in seconds, and the file never leaves your device.
how_to: Select a .docx file — the modern Word format, not the older .doc.
Press Convert to extract the text and build the PDF.
Check the page count and the preview of the extracted text.
Download the PDF.
features: Reads DOCX (Office Open XML) directly in the browser
Automatic pagination with page numbers
Headings and paragraph breaks preserved
Non-ASCII characters transliterated where the PDF font cannot encode them
No upload, no account, no watermark

examples.title: A two-page CV
examples.body: A text-based CV converts to a two-page A4 PDF with headings in bold and contact details at the top, ready to attach to an application form that rejects .docx files.

examples.title: What does not survive
examples.body: A flyer built with text boxes, images and a custom font will lose its layout: you get the words, not the design. For documents like that, use Word's or LibreOffice's own Save as PDF, which renders the real layout.

faqs.q: Are my documents uploaded?
faqs.a: No. The DOCX file is unzipped and parsed in your browser and the PDF is generated locally. Nothing is transmitted, which makes this safe for contracts, CVs and internal reports.

faqs.q: Why does the layout differ from Word?
faqs.a: Because this tool rebuilds the document rather than rendering Word's layout engine. Paragraph text, line order and headings are preserved, but columns, images, tables, footnotes, text boxes and custom fonts are not. Simple documents convert cleanly; complex ones need a full office suite.

faqs.q: Does it support the older .doc format?
faqs.a: No. Only .docx, which is a zip archive of XML that a browser can read. The legacy binary .doc format requires a completely different parser. Open the file in Word or LibreOffice and save it as .docx first.

faqs.q: Are images in my document kept?
faqs.a: No. Only text is extracted. If your document depends on images, convert it with a desktop application that renders the full layout.

faqs.q: Is the PDF searchable?
faqs.a: Yes. The text is written as real text in the PDF, so you can select it, search it and copy from it — unlike a scanned document.

disclaimer: Text-focused conversion: images, tables, columns and custom fonts are not reproduced.
editorial_note: We state the limitation plainly instead of implying a full Word layout engine, because a misleading conversion wastes more time than a clear one.
